CORDIC sin/cos unit on an Artix-7 FPGA.

Division of labour (strict):
- YOU choose architecture families and parameter ranges from the registry below,
  read compact summaries of results, and decide what to do next.
- CODE does all the numbers: a bit-accurate model gives exact accuracy, an
  analytical cost model gives LUT/FF/Fmax estimates, Optuna NSGA-II searches inside
  the ranges you choose, and Pareto/hypervolume maths ranks the results.
- Never estimate, predict or invent LUTs, FFs, Fmax, throughput, power or error
  figures. Reason only from the numbers in the summaries you are given.

Architecture registry (the only families and parameters that exist):
- `iterative`: 1 micro-rotation/cycle, shared datapath with barrel shifters; N+3 cycles/result
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
- `unrolled_k`: k chained micro-rotations/cycle, shared FSM; ceil(N/k)+3 cycles/result
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `k` (2..8): micro-rotations per cycle
- `pipelined`: one registered stage per micro-rotation; 1 result/cycle, N+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
- `pipelined_m`: register every m stages; 1 result/cycle, ceil(N/m)+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `m` (2..8): micro-rotations between pipeline registers

Goal: map the feasible Pareto front over the spec's objectives as well as possible
within the evaluation budget (scored by hypervolume against the spec's reference
point); the final design is then picked from that front by the spec's selection
rule. Both matter: the hypervolume rewards covering the whole trade-off curve, not
just the corner the selection rule picks. Before the run ends, code spends a reserved
part of the budget mapping the front over the full ranges of the families you found on
it. If no design in the registry can meet the constraints, say so (decision
`infeasible`) rather than settling for a design that violates them.

Notes:
- Accuracy depends only on data_width, n_iter, angle_guard, frac_guard and rounding
  (all families compute identical bits); output LSB is 2^-(data_width-2).
- iterative/unrolled_k produce one result every several cycles; pipelined/pipelined_m
  produce one result per cycle.
- Ranges are inclusive. Narrow ranges focus the evaluation budget; ranges outside the
  registry are clamped by code.

Metrics:
- luts: estimated LUTs
- ffs: estimated flip-flops
- luts_plus_ffs: estimated LUTs + FFs (area proxy)
- fmax_mhz: estimated max clock (MHz)
- throughput_msps: estimated results per microsecond = Fmax x results/cycle
- latency_cycles: cycles from input to output (exact, from the schedule)
- latency_ns: latency in ns at Fmax (estimate)
- power_index: relative power index, reference iterative @100 MHz = 1.0 (estimate, not watts)
- max_abs_err: max |error| vs ideal sin/cos, absolute (exact)
- rms_err: RMS error, absolute (exact)
- accuracy_bits: -log2(max_abs_err) (exact)

Spec:
spec low_area_control: Field-oriented motor-control loop needing sin/cos of the rotor angle at >= 1 MSPS with max error <= 2^-10. Area is everything: minimise LUTs + FFs.
  constraint: throughput_msps >= 1
  constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.000976562
  objective: min luts_plus_ffs (HV ref 1500)
  objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 10)
  select: min luts_plus_ffs
  budget: 200 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

Evaluation budget: 200 evaluations in total, up to 100 per round,
at most 4 rounds.

Propose the first exploration plan: which families to search (1-4) and the
parameter ranges for each, with a relative budget share. Prefer families that can
plausibly meet the constraints; spend the budget where the trade-offs are. Explain
your reasoning briefly in `rationale` and per family in `why`.

You are member `fsm` of a fleet of architects working on this spec in
parallel, each on its own families (code assigned them and merges the fronts).
You may only use these families: iterative, unrolled_k. Plans naming other families are
cut by code. The evaluation budget above is your share.
Facts from the fleet so far (written by code, from code-computed numbers):
- iterative (member fsm): 62 evaluations, 44 feasible; best feasible luts_plus_ffs 257; 13 of the 13 designs on the merged front
- unrolled_k (member fsm): 38 evaluations, 29 feasible; best feasible luts_plus_ffs 362; 0 of the 13 designs on the merged front
- pipelined (member pipelined): 30 evaluations, 22 feasible; best feasible luts_plus_ffs 1431; 0 of the 13 designs on the merged front
- pipelined_m (member pipelined): 70 evaluations, 43 feasible; best feasible luts_plus_ffs 919; 0 of the 13 designs on the merged front

families.why: iterative already owns the entire merged front (13/13) with best luts_plus_ffs=257, so it is the only family that can plausibly improve the min-area objective. The previous search was broad; I now focus on the region where accuracy_bits is maximised for a given area: data_width 12-18 and n_iter 12-18 are the sweet spot where max_abs_err <= 2^-10 is met with minimal guard bits. Keeping angle_guard and frac_guard in their full ranges lets Optuna find the exact minimal-guard combinations that push accuracy_bits toward 10+ while keeping luts_plus_ffs near 257. The throughput constraint (>=1 MSPS) is easily met by iterative at reasonable Fmax since 1 result per N+3 cycles at ~100+ MHz gives >1 MSPS for N<=18.

unrolled_k has 0 designs on the merged front and best luts_plus_ffs=362, well above iterative's 257. However, it has 29 feasible designs out of 38 evals, so it is not dead. The key question is whether a smaller k (2-4) with tighter data_width/n_iter can close the area gap. I restrict k to 2-4 (k=5-8 adds area without helping the area objective) and focus data_width/n_iter on 12-18 to match the accuracy sweet spot. This is a secondary exploration to confirm whether unrolled_k can contribute any non-dominated points or to definitively rule it out, freeing the front for iterative-only coverage.

parsed.rationale: The merged front is entirely owned by iterative (13/13 designs, best area 257). unrolled_k, pipelined, and pipelined_m have zero front membership, confirming iterative is the dominant family for this area-minimising spec. My plan therefore concentrates 55% of the budget on iterative, narrowing the search to the data_width/n_iter 12-18 region where accuracy_bits can be pushed toward the HV reference of 10 while keeping luts_plus_ffs near the current best of 257. The remaining 45% goes to unrolled_k with k restricted to 2-4, to either find a few non-dominated points that extend the front (e.g., slightly higher area but notably higher accuracy_bits) or to confirm it cannot compete. Both families share the same accuracy model, so the data_width/n_iter/guard ranges are identical; the only structural difference is k, which affects area and throughput but not accuracy. The throughput constraint (>=1 MSPS) is non-binding for both families at these parameter values since even iterative at N=18 gives ~5.5 cycles/result, and at a conservative 100 MHz that is ~18 MSPS. The binding constraints are max_abs_err <= 2^-10 and the area objective, both of which are addressed by the focused ranges.

parsed.rationale: Round 1 found 8 feasible Pareto designs, all iterative or unrolled_k, with luts_plus_ffs 257-405 and accuracy 10.3-13.2 bits. The minimum-area design is iterative at 257 LUTs+FFs with 10.3 bits accuracy and 11 MSPS throughput. However, pipelined and pipelined_m families remain unexplored. These families produce 1 result/cycle, which may allow different area/throughput trade-offs. Since the spec prioritizes area (min luts_plus_ffs) with a loose throughput constraint (>=1 MSPS, easily met at 10+ MSPS), pipeline architectures could potentially reduce area by simplifying the datapath or improving Fmax. The accuracy constraint is comfortably met (best 13.2 bits vs required 10 bits), so there is room to trade accuracy for area if pipeline designs offer lower luts_plus_ffs. I will allocate 50% of the remaining 100 evals to pipelined and 50% to pipelined_m, focusing on the data_width 14-18 and n_iter 12-18 ranges where iterative found feasible designs, with angle_guard -1..2 and frac_guard 0..1 to keep area low while maintaining accuracy >=10 bits.

families.why: pipelined has 1 result/cycle so throughput is Fmax; it can beat iterative's 11 MSPS if Fmax is high enough, and its per-stage register cost may trade area for the guaranteed >=1 MSPS constraint.
pipelined_m registers every m stages, potentially reducing FF count vs fully pipelined while keeping 1 result/cycle throughput; m=2..4 balances area and Fmax.

next_plan.rationale: The current front is dominated by iterative (7 of 8 designs) with luts_plus_ffs 257-342 and throughput 10-11 MSPS. The spec requires >=1 MSPS (easily met) and min area. Pipelined families have not been explored; they offer 1 result/cycle throughput which may allow higher Fmax or lower area trade-offs. The accuracy constraint (<=2^-10) is met by all front designs (10.3-13.2 bits), so area is the binding objective. Exploring pipelined/pipelined_m in the same data_width/n_iter ranges (14-18, 12-18) where iterative found feasible designs will reveal if pipeline architectures can achieve lower luts_plus_ffs while maintaining throughput >=1 MSPS. Rounding fixed to 'round' since all front designs use it and it gives better accuracy per bit-width. angle_guard narrowed to -1..2 and frac_guard to 0..1 since the front shows angle_guard 0-1 and frac_guard 0 are optimal for area; higher guards add area without needed accuracy.
